statuses.ready: no reveal yet, no mines placed
statuses.playing: mines placed at the first reveal
statuses.won: every safe cell revealed; all mines auto-flagged; timer frozen
statuses.lost: a mine revealed (reveal or chord); exploded cells marked; timer frozen

actions.reveal: no-op on revealed/flagged cells; first reveal places mines outside the clipped 3x3 block; zero cells flood iteratively; flags stay hidden
actions.flag: toggle on hidden cells; no-op on revealed cells; flags may exceed the mine count
actions.chord: on a revealed number whose adjacent flag count matches: opens the other hidden unflagged neighbours; wrong flags detonate; otherwise a no-op

game.revisions: Every state-changing action or deduction batch increments the revision by exactly 1; no-ops and errors never mutate. Each action carries the revision it was based on.
game.validation_order: action -> coordinates (integers) -> bounds -> revision type -> stale -> game over; deductions: revision/stale/over -> not started -> index range -> distinct hidden cells. All validation precedes mutation.
game.observation: Solver input = clue value of every revealed safe cell; never flags, the layout or unrevealed clues.
game.timer: Starts at the first reveal, frozen at win/loss; baseline rounds seconds to 3 decimals, i.e. integer milliseconds on the injected monotonic clock.

statuses.exact: every component counted; 0/1 only for proven cells

meta.decision_49: Real solver statuses (exact, approximate, unavailable) carry effective_sample_size as null when C masks it and as a number when present, alongside the three count diagnostics; optional diagnostics are omitted only for the ready/finished placeholders (not-started, finished).

proof_rules: Exact: integer numerator 0 proves safe, numerator == Z proves mine; never from rounding.
Exact non-certain ratios never convert to 0.0/1.0 (smallest subnormal / 1-2^-53 guard).
Approximate/unavailable: proofs only from propagation or exhaustively counted components; sampled endpoints never prove.

message_templates.exact: Exact probabilities for {hidden} unrevealed cells ({frontier} next to clues in {components} group(s), {pool} unconstrained).
message_templates.approximate: Approximate probabilities: exact counting exceeded the budget for {hard} of {components} group(s), estimated from {samples} weighted samples (effective sample size {ess:.0f}). Only logically proven cells are marked certain.

reason_text.sampling_budget_exhausted: no sampling budget was left for the hard component(s)
reason_text.no_consistent_samples: sampling found no consistent layout for a component
reason_text.no_globally_compatible_samples: no sampled layouts could be combined to match the mine total
reason_text.insufficient_effective_samples: too few effective samples for a reliable estimate
reason_text.time_budget_exhausted: the time budget ran out before the result was complete

message_templates.not_started: No mines have been placed yet. They are placed on your first reveal, and that cell and all of its neighbors are guaranteed to be safe.
message_templates.finished: This game is over (you {won|lost}), so there are no odds to show.

engine_service.result_validation: Before caching or applying proofs: status in {exact, approximate, unavailable}; one value per cell; revealed cells null; exact/approximate complete for hidden cells; values finite in [0,1]; proof indices in range, distinct lists, hidden cells, value 0/1 respectively; meta counts non-negative; elapsed finite non-negative; diagnostics valid when present. Failures become probability_failed: nothing applied or cached.
engine_service.cache: Exact and approximate results cached for the current revision only; no-ops keep the cache; changes and batches clear it; unavailable and failures are never cached (retry recomputes).
engine_service.autosolve: One batch per call: solve (or reuse cache) for the current revision, apply proven mines as flags, clear flags on proven-safe cells, reveal them (with flood), one revision; never guesses; refuses ready (game_not_started) and finished (game_over) games; stale proofs rejected.
engine_service.concurrency: Every async request carries game generation, revision and request generation; the adapter and C both reject mismatches; obsolete solves are cancelled by recreating the solver worker only.

findings.detail: tests.test_probability.SamplingTests.test_injected_rng_makes_sampling_deterministic and test_default_rng_is_reproducible use random_observation(11), which propagation fixes completely (0 components, 0 samples, exact). They never exercise the sampler. Port them with SAMPLING_CASE_RANDOM_SEED_134_SAMPLED, which really samples.
findings.resolution: test_probability.c 'sampling is deterministic for a seed; the default seed is the observation's' solves SAMPLING_CASE_RANDOM_SEED_134_SAMPLED and asserts an approximate result with samples > 0 before comparing seeds (executed in gate-c-final).

findings.detail: test_large_connected_component_is_time_bounded returns unavailable/no_consistent_samples at both 0.3 s and 1.0 s at baseline (5/5 evidence seeds), so its 'approximate' branch is untested; approximate paths are covered by the mixed and random sampling cases.
findings.resolution: Not a migration gap: approximate results are exercised by the seed-134, mixed and node-budget cases; the lattice sampling rows keep the baseline's accepted statuses.

findings.detail: Baseline asserts wall-clock bounds (elapsed < 3.0 s, < budget + 0.5 s). Deterministic C budget tests should use the injected fake clock; keep wall-clock bounds only as generous responsiveness checks.
findings.resolution: C budget tests run on injected fake clocks ('time budgets: phase deadlines on a fake clock', 'deadline injection at every clock check: valid, sound answers'; runtime 'injected clock is finite and monotonic'). Wall-clock bounds remain only in the @solver browser responsiveness checks.

findings.detail: Python integers never truncate. Fixtures add C cases at 2^32+1 (revision), 2^32/2^32+1/10^18 (coordinates), 2^32+9/2^32+10 (config) and 2^32+16 (deduction index); the adapter must also reject unsafe JavaScript integers instead of wrapping them.
findings.resolution: The C harnesses map out-of-range fixture integers to UINT32_MAX (coordinates, configuration) and MS_REVISION_MAX (revisions). The adapter rejects non-integer and unsafe numbers before marshalling (engine-client 'createGame rejects values that would truncate, before marshalling', 'actions reject non-integer arguments before marshalling', 'revisions above the maximum are stale, never wrapped'; abi 'isU32 rejects everything that would truncate into an i32 parameter') and refuses any proof list, 2^32+16 included, in autosolve.

findings.detail: server._normalize_solver_result accepts any string as meta.reason. The C engine validates the reason enumeration (ENGINE_RESULT_CASES/reason_out_of_range).
findings.resolution: engine_results/reason_out_of_range (gate-c-1) and abi 'malformed results are refused' (reason 10).

findings.detail: calculate_probabilities accepts any width/height >= 1; baseline tests rely on 3001x1, 72x1, 18x1 and 3x1 boards. The C solver API must accept such thin boards independently of the 5..80 game limits.
findings.resolution: 'degenerate shapes: 1x1, 1x2, 6400x1 and 1x6400 boards', '3001-cell chain is exact without recursion' and the thin PROBABILITY_CASES rows run through the C solver (executed in gate-c-final).

findings.detail: The server merged duplicate proof indices (ENGINE_RESULT_CASES/proofs_normalized). A C engine may normalise or reject duplicates but must never apply a cell twice; the choice should be documented in engine.h.
findings.resolution: engine.h documents that result proofs are per-cell flag bits, so no cell is applied twice, and that deduction lists may repeat a cell as Python's sets did. engine_results/proofs_normalized and 'deductions: list checks, duplicates, wrong proofs use REVEAL semantics' assert both (gate-c-1).

findings.detail: Reference doubles are correctly rounded (Python int division) and the baseline compares some values for exact equality (corner 1/3 and 1999/6396). Bit-exact native/WASM parity is simplest with a correctly rounded ratio conversion; otherwise compare within 1e-12.
findings.resolution: Reference doubles are compared bit for bit (check_exact_case; 'huge binomials cancel exactly; near-certain cells are not proofs' for 1/3 and 1999/6396; bigint 'ratios: fixtures, endpoint guard, ESS, subnormals, overflow, ties, literals'; 'deterministic results are bit-identical on every runtime').
